nodes.summary: Attainment: when a saturated graph exists, some saturated graph has exactly `sat(n, H)` edges.
nodes.title: Saturation number is attained by a saturated graph

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph. A simple graph $G$ is $H$-saturated if and only if $G$ is $H$-free and every simple graph $G'$ on the same vertex set with $G \subsetneq G'$ contains a copy of $H$.
nodes.title: Saturation via strict supergraphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph. A simple graph $G$ is $H$-saturated if and only if $G$ is $H$-free and, for all distinct vertices $s$ and $t$ of $G$ that are not adjacent in $G$, the graph $G + st$ obtained from $G$ by adding the edge $st$ contains a copy of $H$.
nodes.title: Saturation via missing edges

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph. The complete graph on any vertex set is $H$-saturated if and only if it is $H$-free.
nodes.title: Saturation of complete graphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph. A simple graph $G$ is $H$-saturated if $G$ is $H$-free (it contains no copy of $H$ as a subgraph) and is maximal with this property: every $H$-free simple graph $G'$ on the same vertex set as $G$ with $G \subseteq G'$ equals $G$.
nodes.title: $H$-saturated graphs

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $G$ be simple graphs. A pair of vertices $x, y$ of $G$ is an $F$-saturating non-edge of $G$ if $x \ne y$, $x$ and $y$ are not adjacent in $G$, and the graph $G + xy$ obtained from $G$ by adding the edge $xy$ contains a copy of $F$ (a subgraph isomorphic to $F$, not necessarily induced).
nodes.title: Saturating non-edge

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $G$ be simple graphs, and let $xy$ be an $F$-saturating non-edge of $G$. If $G$ is $F$-free, that is, $G$ contains no copy of $F$, then the graph $G + xy$ obtained from $G$ by adding the edge $xy$ contains a copy of $F$, and $G$ does not.
nodes.title: A saturating non-edge of an $F$-free graph creates a copy of $F$

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $G$ be simple graphs such that $G$ has only finitely many $F$-saturating non-edges. Then $f_F(G)$ is the number of $F$-saturating non-edges of $G$, counted as unordered pairs $\{x, y\}$, that is, the number of edges of the graph of $F$-saturating non-edges of $G$.
nodes.title: Number of saturating non-edges

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph and $n$ a natural number. The set of saturated edge counts of $H$ on $n$ vertices is the set of natural numbers $m$ such that some $H$-saturated simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ has exactly $m$ edges.
nodes.title: Edge counts of saturated graphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph, $n$ a natural number, and $\operatorname{sat}(n, H)$ the saturation number of $H$ on $n$ vertices. If the set of saturated edge counts of $H$ on $n$ vertices is empty, that is, no $H$-saturated simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ exists, then $\operatorname{sat}(n, H) = 0$.
nodes.title: The saturation number is zero when no saturated graph exists

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph, $n$ a natural number, and $\operatorname{sat}(n, H)$ the saturation number of $H$ on $n$ vertices. Every $H$-saturated simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ has at least $\operatorname{sat}(n, H)$ edges.
nodes.title: Saturated graphs bound the saturation number

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph and $n$ a natural number. The saturation number $\operatorname{sat}(n, H)$ is the minimum number of edges of an $H$-saturated simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$, and is $0$ when no such graph exists.
nodes.title: Saturation number

nodes.summary: Let $F$ and $G$ be simple graphs. The graph of $F$-saturating non-edges of $G$ is the simple graph on the vertices of $G$ whose edges are exactly the $F$-saturating non-edges of $G$.
nodes.title: Graph of saturating non-edges

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
